measure.measure_definition: Partial Mayo Clinic score (pMCS), scale 0–9, with higher scores indicating more severe ulcerative-colitis activity. Assessed at baseline and week 6 in the primary ITT/BOCF analysis. This is the continuous disease-activity score; clinical remission uses the separate pMCS ≤1 criterion M4.

Occurrence: proportion of participants with clinical remission (pMCS ≤1) at week 6; Participants; pMCS assessed at week 6; clinical remission defined by pMCS ≤1. Intention-to-treat analysis with BOCF for missing week-6 outcomes.; Clinical remission threshold pMCS ≤1 at week 6; participants meeting the threshold counted as remitters. Higher pMCS indicates worse disease activity.

Fecal calprotectin (FC) normalization at week 6, defined as stool FC ≤150 μg/g. FC was assessed at baseline and week 6; the relevant baseline-FC populations are P3 (SCD) and P4 (MeD). Reported normalization counts/proportions and the comparison test quantify this threshold-defined outcome.

population.intervention_regimen: Not reported (calories tailored to individual energy requirements; no drug dose applicable); Exclusive SCD for 6 weeks; three meals and two snacks per day prepared by the MGH Metabolic Kitchen; weekly dietitian visits; additional 4-week follow-up after the intervention.
population.population_definition: Randomized diet allocation to SCD; intention-to-treat.; Adults aged 18–75 years with confirmed ulcerative colitis and active disease for at least 3 months before screening, pMCS 2–6, randomized 1:1 to SCD. Key exclusions included Crohn's disease, severe or fulminant UC, prior colectomy or ostomy, and recent antibiotic use. All randomized SCD participants were included in the intention-to-treat analysis.
population.population_time_frame: Enrolment September 3, 2020 to April 19, 2023; intervention baseline to week 6; follow-up to week 10.
